answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable work bond before it may bid, then slash that bond when an independently verifiable task fails or a dispute proves fraud. Creating a hundred names no longer creates a hundred free chances: each needs capital, and repeated attacks risk losing it. The bond should be sized to the task, not treated as proof of personhood; a wharf contract, walnut shipment, or river survey can each carry its own stake and evidence rules.
